segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Hello Charlotte. I’m Kaeden, one of the supervisors. Welcome to the team.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Hi Aiden.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: It’s Kaeden.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I’m so sorry.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Don’t worry. People often get my name wrong; they never know how to spell it. It’s K-A-E-D-E-N, in case you ever need to write it.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I’ll try and remember.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: So, there are a few practical things you need to sort out this morning. Then I’ll show you what you’re going to do today.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: The email I received said to go to the front desk, to show my letter of appointment and pick up my badge.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: You’ll need that for the staffroom and other areas of the supermarket where shoppers aren’t allowed. So, after you’ve finished at the front desk, I’ll take you to the staffroom. Put your coat and rucksack in one of the lockers there. Take whichever one is free.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Will I have a key?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Yes. Try not to lose it. At the end of the day, leave it in the door for the next person to use.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Will do.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: You also need to go to the HR department to see Tiffany. She’s really helpful.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I was told to bring my passport with me. HR need to take a note of the number in it.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: That’s right. Or you can show your ID card.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I don’t have one of those.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: OK. Tiffany will give you a uniform. They have lots in different sizes, so you just tell her what you need. I won’t come with you to HR – I’ve got to go and sort something else out. Problem with a bread slicer.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Is the HR office near the staffroom?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: The staffroom’s on the first floor, and HR are a couple of floors above that, on the third floor. There’s a staircase outside the staffroom.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: When you’ve finished with HR, come and find me in the bakery section of the shop.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I’m looking forward to getting started.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: I’ll just give you my phone number, in case you can’t find me. Have you got your phone there?

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Yes ... OK, ready.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: It’s oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: OK, done.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: So, Charlotte, your tasks today are in the bakery section, on the sushi counter, and on the meat and fish counters. The first job is to check sell-by dates on the bread and cakes. If any of the dates are today’s, put a new price label on the packaging.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: What if any of the labels are yesterday’s dates, or older? Do I throw those items away?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Yes, but that shouldn’t happen – we check the stock every day. When something needs a new price label, put a yellow one on the package, next to the original price.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: After that, you’ll go to the sushi takeaway counter.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Will I be preparing boxes of food?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: For today, you’ll just be helping the staff.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Yes, of course.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: You’ll see lots of flat cardboard boxes at one end of the counter. Beneath those is where we keep the plastic boxes -we run out of those really quickly, so you should bring more from the storeroom.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Is that my only task on the sushi counter?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: No. You also need to clean the area where they prepare the dishes. There are cloths and bottles of spray by the sink. Oh, and please make sure you clean that too.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Sure. That’s important, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Absolutely. But you mustn’t wash up knives. You have to do some training before you’re allowed to touch sharp objects.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: What should I do if there are any?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Ask someone to put them in the dishwasher.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: OK, thanks. I don’t want to get anything wrong.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Don’t worry. You’ll be fine. And I’ll be around to help.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: Finally, the meat and fish counters. You need to clean the area where staff serve customers, including wiping the weighing scales.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: OK. Anything else?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: The fish is laid on ice, but when that starts to melt, you’ll need to get more from the cold-room.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: I know the staff on the food counters wear a hat. Will that be the same for me?

segments.speaker: KAEDEN
segments.en: You won’t be serving customers directly, so no. But make sure you put on thermal gloves when you take anything out of the cold-room. The temperature’s low enough in there to get frostbite from touching things.

segments.speaker: CHARLOTTE
segments.en: Understood.
